candidates.name: FILE_STREAM_INFO
verified_facts: Enumerates named data streams, their logical sizes, allocation sizes, and linked-entry offsets for a file handle.
semantic_limits: Stream presence and allocation are file-system-specific and do not prove content identity or authorized producer.

candidates.name: FILE_NAME_INFO
verified_facts: Returns a handle-relative file name and byte length through a variable-size buffer.
semantic_limits: A returned name can be namespace-relative and must be joined to handle, volume, final path, and file ID.

candidates.name: FILE_COMPRESSION_INFO
verified_facts: Returns compressed size, format, and compression-unit geometry for a file handle.
semantic_limits: Compression metadata does not prove byte equality, semantic validity, or receipt provenance.

candidates.name: FILE_STORAGE_INFO
verified_facts: Returns storage characteristics such as logical and physical bytes per sector for a file.
semantic_limits: Reported geometry is a storage snapshot and does not uniquely identify the device or file contents.

candidates.name: FILE_ALIGNMENT_INFO
verified_facts: Returns the required buffer-alignment mask for I/O to a file handle.
semantic_limits: Alignment requirements are operational constraints, not evidence of task ownership or content validity.

candidates.name: FILE_REMOTE_PROTOCOL_INFO
verified_facts: Returns remote protocol and capability information for a remote file handle.
semantic_limits: Protocol capability flags do not prove the remote endpoint, share, file, or receipt is authentic.

candidates.name: FILE_ID_BOTH_DIR_INFO
verified_facts: Returns directory-entry metadata, short names, attributes, sizes, and file IDs in linked records.
semantic_limits: Directory enumeration is a point-in-time view and must be correlated with open-handle identity and timestamps.

candidates.name: FILE_FULL_DIR_INFO
verified_facts: Returns directory-entry times, sizes, attributes, extended-attribute size, and file names.
semantic_limits: Directory-entry metadata can race with changes and does not prove file bytes or producer identity.

candidates.name: FILE_ID_EXTD_DIR_INFO
verified_facts: Returns extended directory information including a 128-bit file identifier when supported.
semantic_limits: A file identifier is volume-scoped and must be paired with volume identity, handle state, and time.

candidates.name: FindFirstStreamW
verified_facts: Starts enumeration of the first ::$DATA stream for a file or directory.
semantic_limits: Stream enumeration can be unsupported or incomplete on some file systems and does not validate stream bytes.

candidates.name: FindNextStreamW
verified_facts: Continues a stream enumeration and returns the next WIN32_FIND_STREAM_DATA record.
semantic_limits: Enumeration order is not identity evidence and the search can race with concurrent stream changes.

candidates.name: WIN32_FIND_STREAM_DATA
verified_facts: Carries a stream size and stream name returned by stream-enumeration functions.
semantic_limits: The record is descriptive metadata only and must be paired with exact file, volume, and content digests.

candidates.name: File Streams
verified_facts: Defines default and named stream syntax and file-system-specific alternate data stream behavior.
semantic_limits: Stream syntax or presence does not establish whether a stream is expected, safe, or task-authorized.

candidates.name: Sparse Files
verified_facts: Explains sparse allocation where storage is committed only to selected nonzero regions.
semantic_limits: Sparse state and logical size do not reveal all physical allocation details or prove byte integrity.

candidates.name: Sparse File Operations
verified_facts: Documents support checks and sparse-file allocation inspection and mutation controls.
semantic_limits: Only read-only inspection is admissible here; no sparse-state or zero-range mutation is performed.

candidates.name: FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES
verified_facts: Returns ranges that may contain nonzero data within a requested file or alternate-stream interval.
semantic_limits: Returned ranges are allocation hints, can be incomplete by buffer, and do not prove actual byte values.
